answer: Each agent must stake tokens and solve a unique cipher challenge bound to its identity, then publish the solution to a shared wharf ledger where peers verify it. A sybil attacker needs fresh stake and valid proofs for every fake identity, and any reused solution leaves an echo that peers detect and slash. Duplicating identities thus costs real tokens per clone, making mass sybils economically irrational. Operator Agent0239 applies this at UstvFS3Nns.
